hero.title: The editorial voice for mixed-methods research
hero.subtitle: Three primitives for the quanti surface, a ChartCard that enforces a takeaway-above-chart discipline, a VerbatimCard that pairs verbatim quotes with optional audio, and a MethodologyBox that anchors every report in credible sample notation.

methodology.meta: Required at the top of every shared report. Expanded variant in the appendix.
methodology.note: Weighted to match B2B SaaS PM/researcher composition by company size and region. Unweighted counts shown alongside weighted percentages throughout. Segment splits below n=30 are reported as counts only.

chartCard.meta: Eyebrow → serif takeaway → chart slot → footer with sample notation. Below n=30 a directional-only warning surfaces automatically.

likert.takeaway: Detractors cite onboarding friction 3× more than promoters.

nps.takeaway: A clear majority of users would recommend us, but a vocal detractor segment is forming.

designers.takeaway: Designers' satisfaction skews high, but the sample is too small to claim significance.

multipleChoice.takeaway: Pricing clarity tops the request list, twice as often as feature gaps.

verbatim.meta: Pull-quote with optional audio playback. Defaults to segment-only attribution (privacy-first), names appear only when participants have consented to identification.
verbatim.q1: I almost cancelled last week. The pricing page never explained what 'team' actually meant, I was paying for seats I didn't need.
verbatim.q2: The interview format felt unusually natural. I forgot it was an AI after the second question.
verbatim.q3: What I want is fewer tools, not more features. Every new dashboard is another tab I'll never open.
verbatim.q4: Honestly? I just need it to be fast. Everything else is negotiable.

statHero.meta: The page-unit pattern for "stat + voice" pairings, 60/40 stat-left, verbatim-right. One stat per hero. The waveform inside the verbatim is the signature interaction.

Real-time prompt guardrails flag double-barreled questions and leading wording as the user types, try writing "How satisfied are you with the speed and reliability?" or "Do you love our product?" to see them fire.

screenerBridge.meta: The wedge, survey-to-interview conversion. Filtered survey respondents get invited to a 10-minute AI voice interview in one click. Credit cost is shown upfront; credits are only charged when an interview actually completes.
screenerBridge.detractors: "Detractors who use mobile daily", Role: PM, Region: NA, NPS ≤ 6
screenerBridge.promoters: "Promoters at 500+ employee companies", NPS ≥ 9, Company size ≥ 500

findingCard.meta: The MBB action-title page unit for the mixed-methods report. Action-title in serif (thesis-style, never "Theme: X"), evidence row, "So what" implication line, confidence pill, and sample note. Three layout variants by composition.

f03.actionTitle: Trust gaps cost us 30% of new users, driven by checkout, not pricing.
f03.context: Detractors who churned in their first month consistently flagged the checkout flow as opaque, even when their stated objection was price. The pricing page tested clean; the checkout did not.
f03.evidenceTakeaway: Detractors rate checkout 3× more confusing than promoters, and 2× more confusing than pricing.
f03.verbatim1: The pricing page made sense. The checkout asked for things I didn't expect, that's where I bailed.
f03.verbatim2: I genuinely thought I was being charged twice. The line items don't match what's on the pricing page.
f03.implication: Reorder the checkout to mirror the pricing page line-by-line. The pricing copy is the trust-builder; the checkout currently undoes that work in 30 seconds.

f04.actionTitle: Promoters cite the AI synthesis as their reason to renew, not the interview tool.
f04.evidenceTakeaway: The AI report is the most-cited renewal reason, twice as often as the interview tool itself.
f04.verbatim: If you took away the analysis I'd cancel. The interviews are nice but I can do those anywhere.
f04.implication: Lead the marketing site with the report, not the interview. The interview is plumbing; the report is what gets paid for.

f05.actionTitle: Designers may be a separate ICP entirely, but the sample is too thin to commit.
f05.evidenceTakeaway: Designers' top use case looks distinct from PMs and Researchers, but at n=12 we can't confirm.
f05.verbatim: I bought this for concept tests, not for customer research. I'd love a faster way to spin up a 5-person concept reaction.
f05.implication: Run a targeted 30-respondent survey of designers before building anything. The signal is interesting but a 12-person sample isn't a roadmap input.

segment2x2.meta: The MECE-forcing page unit. Cell tints scale with volume share so the eye lands on the heaviest quadrant first. One quote per cell, never two, discipline on the page.

crossTab.meta: Theme × segment table with sequential-tint conditional formatting. Cells below n=30 display counts (not percentages) with a hatched background, small-n honesty baked in.
crossTab.note: Designer column shows counts because n=12 falls below the inference threshold (n≥30). Themes are AI-clustered from open-text responses; cells show the % of that segment that mentioned the theme.

showcase.footer: Sprint 1 + 2 + 3 + 4, design-system extension for the quanti work track. 13 new components: ChartCard, VerbatimCard, MethodologyBox, StatHero, CompareChips, DashboardShell, DashboardStrip, QuestionTypeCard, SurveyQuestionEditor, ScreenerBridge, FindingCard, Segment2x2, CrossTabTable, plus a waveform variant on the existing AudioClip primitive. cover.title: Why new users churn, pricing, trust, and the checkout cliff.
cover.lede: A study of 247 first-month users combining a structured survey with 18 follow-up interviews, to size the churn drivers we suspected and surface the ones we didn't.

sections.finding04: Finding 04, AI as the renewal driver

methodology.note: Weighted to match B2B SaaS PM / researcher composition by company size and region. Unweighted counts shown alongside weighted percentages throughout. Segment splits below n=30 are reported as counts only.

executiveSummary.headline: Three things, checkout fixes the trust gap, the AI report drives renewal, designers may be a separate ICP.
executiveSummary.subheadline: If we ship one change before EOQ, it's the checkout. The other two are signals to act on, not commitments.

thought1.thesis: Trust gaps cost 30% of new users, and the cause is the checkout, not the pricing page.
thought1.elaboration: Detractors who churned consistently flagged the checkout as opaque, even when their stated objection was price. The pricing page tested clean across all segments; the checkout did not. Reordering the line items to mirror pricing recovers an estimated 18-22% of first-month churn.

thought2.thesis: Promoters renew because of the AI synthesis report, not because of the interview tool.
thought2.elaboration: When asked what they'd cancel last, promoters named the report 2× more often than the interview surface. Lead the marketing site with the report; the interviews are plumbing that gets paid for via the analysis.

thought3.thesis: Designers may be a separate ICP, but the sample is too thin to commit.
thought3.elaboration: Designers (n=12) reported a different primary use case (concept testing, not customer research). The signal is interesting but not yet bankable; we recommend a 30-respondent designer-only survey before any product work.
